title: A Custody Plea Under the Guardians and Wards Act Must Go to the Court Where the Child Lives: Gujarat High Court
citation: Civil Application (For Transfer) No. 1673 of 2025; 2026 LiveLaw (Guj) 291
card_summary: A wife living 300 km away in Rajkot sought to transfer her own custody petition and her husband's matrimonial suit there, citing travel hardship. Justice Maulik Shelat refused, holding a custody petition under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 must be decided where the children actually reside, which was Himmatnagar. Rajkot's family court had no jurisdiction over custody whatever the travel distance.
card_tip: A transfer plea citing travel hardship will not move a custody case out of the court where the children live; the Guardians and Wards Act fixes jurisdiction by the child's residence, not either parent's convenience.
verification_notes: LiveLaw and Verdictum both report the same ruling by Justice Maulik Shelat on the Section 24 CPC transfer applications, the Himmatnagar-Rajkot facts, the wife's hardship argument and the holding that custody jurisdiction follows the children's residence. Citation 2026 LiveLaw (Guj) 291, Civil Application (For Transfer) No. 1673 of 2025, per LiveLaw's weekly round-up for 19-25 October 2026. Exact pronouncement date is reported as around 24 October 2026; neither source gives a more precise date.
